meaning.evidence: All facts survive (10 am, Privy Council, PMBOK quote, agile/scrum/Kanban, same time and place, not a status update, token, 5-15 minutes, XP/scrum names, 2017 questions removed in 2020). Most additions are colour, but "your typical status meeting, where half the room's nodding off" adds a claim, and "what they're going to have a crack at" loses the idea of commitments.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "sort out the curly or slow-going problems", "rock up", "follow-up yarns", "deep-and-meaningfuls", "how they're tracking", "got the chop".

authenticity.evidence: Sounds Australian ("nobody waits around for the stragglers", "big long natters"), though the opener "Pull up a stool. Actually, don't." and "if it's good enough for the King's advisers, it's good enough for your lot" are set-piece gags.

tone.evidence: The encyclopedic explanation becomes a stand-up routine: "Sore feet keep it short.", "half the room's nodding off", "the lot of 'em leg it back to their desks". More gags than the voice change needs.

flow.evidence: Reads well, but the added one-liners at paragraph ends ("Save the deep-and-meaningfuls for later.") interrupt the explanation.

variety.evidence: Varied: "have a crack", "headache", "curly", "rock up", "stragglers", "yarns", "proper mess", "heaps", "chuck in", "deep-and-meaningfuls", "belts through", "natters", "got the chop".

essence.evidence: Recognisably the Wikipedia article, but the added jokes and the "In other words" gloss shift it from reference to banter.

problems.original: to make commitments to team members

A.summary: A lively, varied level-4 retelling that keeps the facts but piles on gags beyond what the article's tone supports.

sense.evidence: Many wrong senses: "swear blind" for resolve, "battlers" for people, "belt goal" and "leg it goal" for sprint goal.

authenticity.evidence: Stage-Australian tags on untouched text: "Tell ya what, the meeting should usually occur", "'daily stand-up', mate", "sprint goal, ay?".

register.evidence: No swearing problems, but the text is mostly the original with a few tags and swaps, far lighter than level 4.

tone.evidence: The neutral article is disrupted by nonsense and tags, even inside the Scrum Guide questions.

B.summary: A broken word-swap pass that mangles the Scrum terminology.

meaning.evidence: Every point survives, including "make commitments to each other", the token, 5-15 minutes, the three 2017 questions verbatim and their removal in 2020.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "hear about any strife coming up", "knock over the tricky or time-chewing problems", "turn into a right mess", "no rabbiting on", "got the flick".

authenticity.evidence: A natural Aussie explainer: "any software development process going", "having their say", "what they reckon they'll be working on till the next one".

tone.evidence: Keeps the informative article tone under the slang; additions like "no rabbiting on" hang off the original.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly; "follow-up chats" repeats once but unobtrusively.

variety.evidence: Varied: "strife", "knock over", "time-chewing", "handy", "turn up", "a yarn", "right mess", "know-how", "chuck in", "rabbiting on", "yakking", "got the flick".

problems.why: "follow-up chats" used twice in consecutive sentences.

problems.quote: any deep-dive yakking about what's in the way
problems.why: "deep-dive" is corporate jargon beside the slang; slight clash.

C.summary: A faithful, natural, varied level-4 retelling that keeps the article's tone.
